units.en: Isaac born; Hagar & Ishmael sent out

entries.kind: the overthrow of Sodom becomes a revolution
entries.comment: וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת־לוֹט מִתּוֹךְ הַהֲפֵכָה — God sent Lot out from the midst of the overthrow (19:29). הֲפֵכָה occurs only here, but its relative מַהְפֵּכָה is the Bible's word for Sodom's fate: מַהְפֵּכַת סְדֹם וַעֲמֹרָה (Deut. 29:22; cf. Amos 4:11). Modern Hebrew kept the root and turned it round: a מַהְפֵּכָה is a revolution, a הַפִּיכָה a coup. The word for a catastrophe that leaves nothing standing now means turning a world over on purpose.

entries.kind: a once-only verb becomes the name of the story
entries.comment: The Torah never calls Genesis 22 a sacrifice of Isaac. Abraham וַיַּעֲקֹד אֶת־יִצְחָק בְּנוֹ, bound his son (22:9), and this is the only use of the root עקד in the Bible. Tradition named the chapter after its single hapax: עֲקֵדַת יִצְחָק. In Modern Hebrew the עֲקֵדָה is shorthand for the sacrifice of sons, above all a generation lost to the nation's wars, and a poem or play on the עקדה is close to a genre.

entries.kind: a test that proves a person becomes an attempt
entries.comment: וְהָאֱלֹהִים נִסָּה אֶת־אַבְרָהָם — God tested Abraham (22:1), a trial that shows what a person is made of. Modern Hebrew uses the same verb for any attempt: נִסִּיתִי, "I tried"; a נִסּוּי is a lab experiment, and נִסָּיוֹן is an attempt and the experience on a CV. Balashon asks whether נֵס, a miracle, is the same family: Abraham's ten trials against Egypt's ten miracles. The Mega Bible annotation cites Ma'agarim (Mendele, 1862, among the early examples) and Ben-Yehuda.

Of Ishmael in the wilderness: וַיְהִי רֹבֶה קַשָּׁת — he became an archer (21:20). קַשָּׁת, "bowman", is a once-only word, and Hagar had sat down כִּמְטַחֲוֵי קֶשֶׁת, a bowshot off (21:16), the parasha's other archery hapax. The participle רֹבֶה, a shooter (its root is debated), is the form Modern Hebrew uses for the weapon: רוֹבֶה is a rifle. The man who shoots gave his name to the thing he shoots with. Sources: Ma'agarim (Mendele, 1862) and Ben-Yehuda.

evidence.title: נתנו בידי רובה כדי להגן על חיי-ולמרבה הצער גם להרוג בשעת סכנה
evidence.gloss: A State Archives sheet whose headline puts a רובה, "rifle", in a soldier's hands "to protect my life, and unfortunately also to kill in a moment of danger." Plain public vocabulary.
evidence.credit: State Archives · National Library of Israel

what Abraham serves with milk → butter (Balashon, "chemah")
"far be it from You" → חַס וְחָלִילָה, God forbid (Balashon, "chalila and chas")
Sodom's brimstone → גַּפְרוּר, a match; Ben-Yehuda's מַדְלֵק lost out (Balashon, "gafrur")
